findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post usernames
findings.body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light-theme branch uses 70% and the dark branch uses 30%, so the two values are swapped. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value for light themes and uses (100−X)% for dark. As written, the default (light) theme now shows these bold usernames much fainter than before. Dark themes get the de-emphasized value where the emphasized one was intended. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 70% to 30% for .custom-message-length
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new code uses 30% for light themes and 70% for dark, so the values are inverted. On the default light theme, the flag custom-message length hint on mobile now renders much darker than before. It is also inconsistent with the desktop rule in desktop/modal.scss, which correctly uses 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 light-theme lightness silently changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` but is now 50%/50%. This changes the default light-theme appearance, making the headers noticeably lighter, which a dark-theme-only fix should not do. The desktop equivalent was correctly converted to 20%/80%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, slightly darker than `.title` at 50% so the name stands out. The conversion uses 50%/50%, which changes the light-theme rendering and removes the visual distinction between name and title. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This is the same issue as on desktop. The original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became 50%/50%, which alters the default light-theme color and makes the member name look the same as the title. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Remaining unconverted scale-color($primary) in categories badge-notification
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%); }` was not converted, unlike every other occurrence in this file. On dark themes `$primary` is light, so lightening it 50% gives a nearly white value. The category topic counts will therefore not match the surrounding converted text, which is the problem this PR is meant to fix. It should use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.
